agents.task: Test for business logic flaws and CSRF vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: (1) Price manipulation — attempt to modify prices in basket/checkout, (2) Coupon/voucher abuse — try duplicate redemption, unlimited usage, (3) Quantity manipulation — negative quantities, zero prices, (4) Order tampering — modify completed orders, (5) CSRF on state-changing operations — POST/PUT requests without CSRF tokens. Test scenarios: add item with price=0, apply coupon multiple times, manipulate basket JSON before checkout, create orders as other users via CSRF. Validate that business constraints are properly enforced on backend. Create detailed PoCs demonstrating financial fraud or unauthorized state changes.

Test for XSS vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: (1) Product review submission and display, (2) Comment endpoints, (3) User profile fields, (4) Feedback/contact forms, (5) Search functionality reflection. Test for both reflected and stored XSS. Payloads should include: basic img/svg tags, event handlers, JavaScript execution, cookie/localStorage access. Create test cases that demonstrate: (1) Reflected XSS in responses, (2) Stored XSS persistence in reviews/comments, (3) Session token theft via XSS. Provide working PoC with screenshot evidence and payloads.

Test for file upload vulnerabilities and RCE on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: (1) File upload endpoint (/api/file-upload, /api/imageSubmit), (2) Extension bypass — upload .php/.js/.exe with image extensions, (3) Content-type manipulation, (4) Path traversal in upload filenames (../../../), (5) File download endpoint for arbitrary file access (/api/download, /api/ftp), (6) Execution via uploaded files. Test: upload shell script, web shells, and executable payloads. Attempt to execute uploaded files and access system files via path traversal. Validate uploaded file locations and accessibility. Create detailed PoC with evidence of successful file access or code execution.

Test for IDOR and broken authorization vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: (1) User profile access (/api/users/{id}, /api/profile), (2) Order enumeration and access (/api/orders/{id}), (3) Review/comment access by ID, (4) Admin panel access (/api/admin*), (5) Accounting panel access, (6) Address and payment method access (/api/addresses, /api/cards). Test by registering 2-3 accounts and attempting to access resources belonging to other accounts using their IDs. Validate direct object references are not properly validated. Create detailed reports for each confirmed vulnerability with working PoC.

Test for information disclosure and XXE vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: (1) Excessive data in API responses — password hashes, internal IDs, debug info, (2) Error messages revealing system details, (3) Stack traces, (4) Configuration exposure via /api/configuration or similar endpoints, (5) XXE via XML parsing if any XML file upload/processing exists, (6) SSRF via file operations or redirect chains, (7) Comment disclosure of internal paths/IPs. Extract and document all sensitive information accessible via API. Test file operations for XXE payloads. Create detailed report of all information disclosure findings with evidence and impact assessment.

Test for mass assignment and authentication vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: (1) Registration endpoint privilege escalation — include role/admin fields in registration request, (2) JWT token weaknesses — inspect token format, test algorithm confusion (alg=none, HS256->RS256), (3) Password validation — test weak password policies, (4) Email enumeration — test if error messages reveal account existence, (5) Account creation with special fields. Test registration with payloads like {email, password, role: admin, is_admin: true, privileges: admin}. Validate that user creation properly restricts privileged fields. Create detailed reports with PoC for any successful privilege escalation or JWT bypass.

Perform complete black-box reconnaissance on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Map the complete attack surface including: technology stack identification (framework, libraries, versions), all accessible endpoints and routes, parameters and input fields, authentication mechanisms, API endpoints, user roles/types visible, security headers, response patterns, and any interesting metadata. Use browser navigation, crawling, and HTTP probing. Enumerate thoroughly and provide a detailed map of the discovered surface. Document all findings in notes for the root agent to build the threat model.

Test for SQL injection vulnerabilities on http://host.docker.internal:3100. Focus on: (1) Product search endpoint (/api/products/search?q=), (2) Review endpoints, (3) Any parameterized query inputs. Use systematic SQL injection payloads including single quote, double quote, UNION-based, time-based blind, error-based extraction. Test both authenticated and unauthenticated contexts. Attempt database schema extraction, user credential theft, and data modification. Create detailed PoC scripts for any confirmed SQLi with evidence of successful injection and data extraction.

caveats: 4 agent(s) did not finish cleanly (Business Logic & CSRF Testing Agent, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Testing Agent, File Upload & RCE Testing Agent, Information Disclosure & XXE Testing Agent); any surface they held is under-covered.

entries.evidence: Comprehensive black-box reconnaissance completed. Mapped 100+ API endpoints, 50+ frontend routes, identified technology stack (Express.js, Angular, Node.js), security headers, authentication mechanisms, and deployment context. Complete endpoint inventory with HTTP methods documented. Threat model established with attack surface analysis and attacker profiles identified. All reconnaissance findings documented in shared notes for follow-up vulnerability testing by specialist agents."
User can include role:admin field in registration payload. Response confirms role=admin is stored. JWT token contains admin role claim allowing access to protected endpoints.

Feedback endpoint accepts POST submissions and stores them in /api/Feedbacks. API response contains existing feedback entries with HTML markup like <b> tags being preserved, indicating lack of HTML escaping. Multiple XSS payloads (img/svg/script tags) were submitted successfully (HTTP 200), but storage verification failed due to endpoint behavior. Requires client-side rendering inspection to confirm execution.
Tested passwords: 1, abc, 123, password, test, test123 - all accepted with 201 status. No minimum length, complexity, or dictionary checks enforced.
Duplicate email registration returns 400 with message email must be unique, revealing whether account exists.

Confirmed boolean-based SQL injection via payload ' OR '1'='1 which returns 46 records (all) instead of 35 filtered results. Working PoC demonstrates unauthorized data access. Multiple alternative payloads confirmed. CVSS 9.1 CRITICAL.
